intro: A fairy tale of about 170 words about a little knight and a dragon, with twelve verbs to fill in — all in the Präteritum, the tense every German story is told in from the first Es war einmal. Each gap gives you only the infinitive; you decide which kind of verb it is and supply the past form with the right ending for the subject. Regular verbs take -te: wohnte, kämpfte, erzählte, lachte. Irregular verbs change their vowel and take no -te: kam, nahm, ritt, sprach, wurden. bringen is a mixed verb (brachte), and sein and haben have their own forms (war, hatten). Watch the subject: der Ritter needs no ending after the stem or -te, die Menschen and die beiden need -en. Read the whole story first, because the story’s logic tells you the verb before the gap does.
tips[0].title: Regular, irregular or mixed? Decide, then form
tips[0].text: wohnen, kämpfen, erzählen, lachen → regular: stem + -te. kommen, nehmen, reiten, sprechen, werden → irregular: vowel change, no -te. bringen → mixed: vowel change and -te (brachte). If unsure, think of the participle: gesprochen, geritten → irregular.
tips[0].check.why: schreiben is irregular (geschrieben): the vowel changes to schrieb and no -te is added.
tips[1].title: The subject decides the ending
tips[1].text: der Ritter / der Drache → er-form: wohnte, kam, brachte (no -t added). die Menschen / die beiden → -en: hatten, wurden. Check the subject of each sentence before you write.
tips[1].trap: English 'had' and 'became' do not change for the plural; German hatte → hatten, wurde → wurden.
tips[1].check.why: The subject die Kinder is plural, so hatte takes -n: hatten. hattet is for ihr.
tips[2].title: The narrative skeleton
tips[2].text: Es war einmal … (opening) · Eines Tages … (the event) · Da … (the turn) · Am Ende … / Seitdem … (the close). Four signposts, and any story has a shape.
tips[2].check.why: Eines Tages ('one day') is the fixed signpost that starts the main event of a story.

remember[0]: Story = Präteritum, from Es war einmal to Am Ende.
remember[1]: Infinitive → regular / irregular / mixed → ending for the subject.
hook: Retell a fairy tale the way German children hear it — Es war einmal … — with every verb in the storytelling past.
